title: Anti-joins and safe de-duplication
objectives: Find rows with no match using NOT EXISTS
Avoid the NOT IN trap when the list holds an empty value
Keep the latest row per key instead of DISTINCT on everything

exercises.prompt: List the customers who have never ordered: customer_id and name, in customer_id order.
hints: The starter returns nothing. One order has an empty customer_id. What is 2 NOT IN (1, 3, NULL)?
NOT EXISTS asks whether any matching order exists, and an empty customer_id never matches.
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id)

exercises.prompt: customer_updates has several rows per customer. Keep only each customer's latest row: customer_id and email, in customer_id order.
hints: DISTINCT removes rows that are identical in every column. Customer 1's two emails aren't identical.
Number each customer's rows newest first with row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC), then keep number 1.
